description: We are ZM Lunar Coders, a two-person youth coding team from Bahrain competing in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. We love space exploration, game design, and programming, and we are building an interactive Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer using NASA open data.
summary:
Artemis Odyssey is an interactive, browser-based 3D mission trainer built for the Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge. Designed for students and young space enthusiasts, the simulator transforms abstract spaceflight physics into a hands-on journey from Earth to Mars with zero downloads required.
Using our interactive Chapter Jump system, trainees pilot five real mission phases: launching aboard NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) from Pad 39B, executing a lunar descent, driving a rover across the Moon's low-gravity surface, landing on Mars, and navigating Martian terrain. A live cockpit HUD tracks real-time velocity, altitude, and G-loads, helping players experience how gravity changes across Earth (1.0g), the Moon (0.16g), and Mars (0.38g).
By combining WebGL 3D graphics with real Artemis mission parameters, Artemis Odyssey empowers classrooms and space camps everywhere to train the next generation of junior astronauts.
details:
Artemis Odyssey is a zero-install 3D browser simulator that teaches students spaceflight physics from Earth to Mars. Using our Chapter Jump menu, trainees pilot five real mission phases—Earth Pad 39B SLS Launch, Moon Landing, Moon Rover Drive, Mars Surface, and Mars Rover Drive—while tracking live velocity, altitude, and G-loads.

Built with HTML5, JavaScript, and WebGL/Three.js and hosted on Netlify, it runs smoothly on any standard school laptop. By pairing real Artemis mission stages and planetary gravity (1.0g Earth, 0.16g Moon, 0.38g Mars) with simple WASD controls, it helps classrooms and space camps train junior astronauts anywhere.
